'''Dieter Seebach''' is a German chemist known for his synthesis of biopolymers and dendrimers, and for his contributions to [[stereochemistry]]. He was born on 31 October 1937 in [[Karlsruhe]]. He studied chemistry at the [[University of Karlsruhe (TH)]] under the supervision of [[Rudolf Criegee]] and at [[Harvard University]] with [[Elias James Corey|Elias Corey]] finishing in 1969. After his [[habilitation]] he became professor for organic chemistry at the [[University of Giessen]]. After six years he was appointed professor at the [[ETH Zurich]] where he worked until he retired in 2003.

==Work==

Seebach worked on [[dendrimer]] chemistry and on the synthesis of [[beta-peptide]]s.<ref>{{cite journal
  | author = Hook, David F.
  | title =  Celebrating Dieter Seebach's Contributions to Science: A Bitter Sweet Occasion?
  | journal = [[Chimia]]
  | volume = 58
  | issue = 2
  | pages =321–324
  | year = 2004
  | doi = 10.2533/000942904777677876
  | doi-access = free
  }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
  | author = Dieter Seebach and Jennifer L. Matthews
  | title =  β-Peptides: a surprise at every turn
  | journal = [[Chem. Commun.]]
  | issue = 21
  | pages = 2015–2022
  | year = 1997
  | doi = 10.1039/a704933a}}</ref> The development of the [[umpolung]], a polarity inversion of the [[carbonyl]] group, with [[1,3-Propanedithiol|1,3-propanedithiol]] together with Corey had a big influence on organic synthesis, and subsequently the [[Corey-Seebach reaction]] was named after them.<ref>{{cite journal
  | author = Seebach D., [[Elias J. Corey|Corey E. J.]]
  | title = Generation and synthetic applications of 2-lithio-1,3-dithianes
  | journal = [[Journal of Organic Chemistry]]
  | volume = 40
  | issue = 2
  | pages = 231–237
  | year = 1975
  | doi = 10.1021/jo00890a018
 }}</ref>

The [[Fráter–Seebach alkylation]], a diastereoselective reaction of beta-hydroxy esters, is named after him.
